I haven't had to use a weapon to defend myself as a civilian and I do not know any other civilians who have. But there are concepts such as "trigger finger frostbite" that can lead to a person freezing up when they have someone in their sights, even if it's a legit "This guy is going to kill/maim me if I do not shoot him" situation.

Empathy is a major factor. Take Che Guevara- he was an executioner. Shot dozens upon dozens of people. But he could never look them in the face when doing it. This is common throughout history, where executioners have difficulty performing the kill when staring into the face, especially the eyes, of the condemned. That's one of the reasons they'd blindfold or put a sack over the condemned's head. Also, think of firing squads- in many cases, some of the shooters would be given blank rounds. This served no other purpose than to make pulling that trigger feel better because they could tell themselves "There's an 80% chance my round was a blank, so I didn't actually kill anyone."

Finally, pre-Skinnerian training, tests by the British determined that less than 1% of soldiers would shoot to kill given the opportunity. And these are soldiers. They would subconsciously shift their aim to intentionally miss or whatever. There's cases documented from WW2: a British scout force was ordered to "hold this hill, and not let any German's through". Germans approached, were spotted, and the Brits dropped their rifles and started throwing rocks and clods of dirt at the Germans. The Germans responded in kind. Nobody was injured or killed.

There are so many variables that go into "How will you react in a self-defense scenario", that it's basically impossible to know for sure how you will react if ever confronted with said scenario. The only thing you can do, is TRAIN. Training greatly increases the odds that you won't think about pulling the trigger in a life-death situation, you'll just do it. Thinking during a fight gets you killed. While you're aiming the gun at Tyrone, looking into his terrified eyes, if you start thinking "Does he have a family? Will this be very painful for him? Maybe he's sorry...", Tyrone is already closing the distance with you to kill you.

TL;DR- Personally, not as a civilian. Training is the only way to avoid "freezing up" in a life/death situation. Look up "trigger finger frostbite" and the Skinner training method.
